data.source_title: Timing and Intensity of Rehabilitation Services During Acute Stroke Hospitalization: Impacts on Functional Recovery and Community Discharge
data.locator: Methods, analytic sample and measures; Results, discharge function models (PT full model). Time to evaluation measured in days from admission to initial therapy evaluation.
data.source_setting: Acute ischemic-stroke hospitalizations across a 13-hospital Colorado health system, including a 678-bed Level I trauma center; OT and PT analyzed separately.
data.source_n: Final analytic samples: PT n=979 and OT n=713; cohorts overlap because many received both disciplines.
data.quantity: Adjusted association of each additional day to PT evaluation with discharge mobility function
data.unit: AM-PAC 6-Clicks mobility score points per additional day
data.source_evidence_basis: In the fully adjusted PT model, an additional day before the initial PT evaluation was associated with a 0.129-point lower discharge mobility score. The endpoint is acute-care discharge function, not an inpatient rehab-facility outcome.
data.limitations: Retrospective observational association in acute stroke care; residual confounding and illness severity may influence timing and function. AM-PAC is not the IRF-PAI measure, and effect should not be interpreted causally or transferred as a rehab-hospital coefficient.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent assessment timing and function tracking as separate process and outcome fields; use the association to motivate local sensitivity analysis only, not to forecast a causal benefit from earlier therapy.

data.source_title: Timing and Intensity of Rehabilitation Services During Acute Stroke Hospitalization: Impacts on Functional Recovery and Community Discharge
data.locator: Results, Table 1; community discharge and admission/discharge AM-PAC function by OT/PT cohort.
data.source_setting: Same acute stroke hospital system; patients receiving OT or PT during hospitalization.
data.source_n: OT cohort n=713; PT cohort n=979; cohorts overlap and are not mutually exclusive.
data.quantity: Community discharge share and mean function scores at admission and discharge, by therapy cohort
data.unit: percent; AM-PAC 6-Clicks score (range 6-24; higher indicates greater independence)
data.source_evidence_basis: The cohort table reports separate community-discharge proportions and admission/discharge function means for OT and PT recipients. These are descriptive outcomes among selected service recipients.
data.limitations: Acute stroke cohort rather than inpatient rehabilitation facility; OT/PT groups overlap and differ by patient mix. These descriptive comparisons cannot estimate discipline effects or serve as local placement probabilities.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Track functional status and discharge destination as distinct outcomes and retain discipline-specific denominators. Require local clinical assessment data before estimating destination transitions.
